newsitem.title: SPAIN: A profile of Spain's Telefonica de Espana.
newsitem.headline: A profile of Spain's Telefonica de Espana.

text.p: Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica de Espana SA will be completely privatised when the state sells its remaining 20.9 percent stake in a share offer on February 18.
A snapshot of the company follows:
(All figures in pesetas for 1995, with the first nine months of 1996 in parentheses)
WHAT: Full-service telecommunications company which says it has the world's largest home market of more than 100 million Hispanic people worldwide
OPERATING INCOME: 1.74 trillion (1.48 trillion, up 13.3 percent)
OPERATING PROFIT: 509.9 billion (414.0 billion, up 8.1 percent)
NET PROFIT: 133.2 billion (120.2 billion, up 19.8 percent)
TOTAL SHARES: 937,470,820
CAPITALISATION: 2.8 trillion at the end of 1996
SHARE OFFER: up to 20.9 percent of capital or 196,738,320 shares
HEADQUARTERS: Madrid

EXECUTIVE BOARD: Chairman Juan Villalonga, board general secretary Javier Revuelta, directors of: finance Fernando Abril; planning Juan Perea; company relations Andres Tejero; and regulation Guillermo Fernandez, who is also in charge of the corporate business unit. Other business unit directors are Rafael Hernandez (residential), Luis Lada (mobile phones), Francisco Mochon (international) and Marcial Portela (Telefonica Internacional-TISA)
AREAS OF BUSINESS: Basic fixed-network telephone service, long distance, mobile telecoms, public services, data transmission, international businesses, multimedia, advertising
NUMBER OF LINES IN SERVICE: 15.9 million in Spain and 27.2 million total including international holdings and mobile telephones (September 1996)
PUBLIC TELEPHONES: 419,000
MOBILE TELEPHONE CLIENTS: 1.7 million in Spain and 800,000 abroad (September 1996)

INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS: more than 8.4 million lines in service, 238,000 cable television clients in Chile and Peru Telefonica's main foreign stakes include 35 percent of CPT-Telefonica del Peru SA, 43.62 percent of Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile-CTC, 18.66 percent of Telefonica de Argentina SA-TASA, 4.88 percent of Compania Anonima de Telefonos de Venezuela-CANTV and 60 percent of the cellular phone firm Telefonica Romania SA
Telefonica also participated in a consortium that won 35 percent of the Brazilian operator Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes-CRT
INTERNATIONAL ALLIANCES: ATT-Unisource, through participation in the joint venture Unisource
EMPLOYEES: 69,570. The number of workers will be cut by 10,000 over the next five years, according to the group's restructuring programme

PRINCIPAL COMPETITORS: Airtel in mobile telephones with 450,000 clients as of October 1996. State television broadcaster Retevision has a licence for basic telephone services and plans to go into operation this year
MARKET REGULATION: The government agreed full liberalisation of the telecommunications market from December 1, 1998, moving the date forward by four years

HISTORY: Telefonica de Espana was set up in 1924 by U.S. group International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation (ITT). In 1946, Telefonica was nationalised by the government of fascist dictator Franco, who later on took all but 33.7 percent of the group public again through a series of issues called "matildes" to minority shareholders.
In October 1995, the state reduced its stake to 21.01 percent after privatising another 10.7 percent tranche. -- Madrid Newsroom + 34 1 585-2167
